e7_s4_rationale: The presence of 4 symmetric concentric ring-shaped opacities in the posterior corneal stroma with smooth surfaces and the absence of deposits, pigmentation, or serrations are characteristic of lattice corneal dystrophy. The imaging studies, including laser scanning in vivo confocal microscopy, also support this diagnosis by revealing long bandlike structures with thin streaks of white lines.

e7_s4_rejected.label: Corneal amyloidosis
e7_s4_rejected.why: Typically presents with irregular, non-ring shaped opacities and often associated with systemic disease, which is not present in this case

e7_s4_rejected.label: Granular corneal dystrophy
e7_s4_rejected.why: Characterized by small, discrete, white-gray opacities in the anterior corneal stroma, which does not match the ring-shaped opacities in the posterior stroma seen in this patient

e7_s4_rejected.label: Schnyder corneal dystrophy
e7_s4_rejected.why: Associated with high cholesterol levels and distinct arcus senilis, which are not present in this case

e7_s4_rejected.label: Thiel-Behnke corneal dystrophy
e7_s4_rejected.why: Typically presents with honeycomb-shaped or fluted corneal opacities, which does not match the ring-shaped opacities seen in this patient
